title: On-demand safety nets and preemption policy notes
body:
Context: quick working notes for an ops-friendly approach to dedicated pool autoscaling + tenant safety nets. Trying to balance predictable latency SLOs for high-tier customers with opportunity to absorb ephemeral spikes from lower-tier tenants without long cold-starts.

Goal (one-liner): define a pragmatic preemption and safety-net policy that reduces customer-visible failures during transient demand while preserving fairness and bounded cost for Redwood.

Why now: we see 3x weekly microbursts from a small subset of tenants that cause SLO regressions for premium customers when shared on the same pool. Dedicated customers expect isolation guarantees, but customers with reserved capacity want to use spare headroom efficiently. Current proposals (see DED-987) are fragmented: many ideas exist — soft quotas, burst credits, pre-warmed slots, fast-preempt lanes — but we need a single coherent operational policy and a rollout experiment plan.

Non-goals: this note does NOT finalize pricing. Not a security design. Not covering private/VPC control plane networking.

High-level principles:
- Protect premium SLOs first: latency p99 target must be met for SLO-bound tenants; degrade opportunistically for non-SLA tiers.
- Predictable preemption: tenants should be able to reason about when and how requests may be throttled or evicted.
- Fast recovery preferred over overprovisioning: safety nets should prioritize short, targeted mitigations (micro-reserves, evict smallest-batched requests) vs long idle warm pools.
- Observability & auditability: every preemption/eviction decision must be traceable and show reason codes, metrics, and affected tokens.

Proposed building blocks (short descriptions):
1) Micro-reserve slots (hot-scratch capacity): tiny pre-warmed containers that sit idle until used for sub-100ms preemption-safe bursts. Charged differently than full reserved GPUs.
2) Burst-credit ledger: tenants accrue burst credit proportional to recent committed usage; credits allow controlled bursts that bypass strict quota gates for short windows. Credits decay on a sliding window to prevent hoarding.
3) Soft-eviction policy w/ graceful degrade: when pressure detected, attempt throttling -> slow-path (lower-cost model variant) -> evict opportunistic tenants (lowest priority, highest cost per token) in that order.
4) Predictive autoscaler with warmstart hints: use short-term demand forecasting (5–15m horizon) with conservative headroom multiplier for high-SLO pools.
5) Tenant fencing: hard isolation lanes where tenants are guaranteed zero cross-tenant interference; configurable by contract.

Detailed behavior (flow):
- Normal steady state: autoscaler maintains target utilization band (60–75% on reserved pools). Micro-reserve count = pool_size * 0.03 (configurable).
- Spike detection: if request queue or P99 latency crosses threshold X for >Y seconds, autoscaler triggers spike mode.
- Spike mitigation sequence:
   a) If tenant has burst credits, allow burst to proceed until credit exhaustion. Emit event BURST_ALLOWED.
   b) If credits exhausted and micro-reserve available, allocate micro-reserve (fast-path). Emit event MICRO_RESERVE_ALLOC.
   c) If both unavailable, attempt model-fallback per-route (route config decides compatible lower-cost model). Emit event MODEL_FALLBACK.
   d) If none work, enact soft-eviction of opportunistic tenants (preemption in order of least-recently-used, smallest active requests first). Emit event SOFT_PREEMPT.<

Preemption rules and guarantees:
- Preemption must be announced to tenant with 30s graceful window where possible (or immediate for interactive requests under overload).
- Evicted requests receive a clear error code (DED_PREEMPTED) + link to docs + reason tag.
- For dedicated SLA lanes, preemption should only occur as last resort; contract must permit temporary queueing or throttling instead.

Observability and metrics (minimum):
- Preemption count by tenant, reason code, latency before/after preemption, tokens lost, burst-credit balance timeline.
- Micro-reserve utilization and warm-start success rate.
- Autoscaler decision log: predicted demand vs actual, headroom multiplier.
- SLOs impact: p50/p95/p99 by tenant and pool.

Operational runbook (ops playbook snippets):
- Pager triggers: p99 latency > SLA target for >2m on premium lane OR >5 soft-preemptions in 10m.
- Immediate steps: check autoscaler logs (predictions), micro-reserve pool status, last 30m of burst-credit changes.
- Short term quick fixes: bump pool headroom by +10% (manual), temporarily disable opportunistic tenants from pool (via tenant-fence toggle), or enable model-fallbacks globally for the pool.

Rollout experiment plan (phases):
- Canary (2 pools): implement micro-reserve + credit ledger, metrics-only mode (emit events but do not preempt) for 2 weeks.
- Pilot (10 pools): enable soft-preemption with long grace windows for non-SLA tenants; monitor false-positive evictions.
- Opt-in (customers): offer "soft-isolation" and "fenced" options in console; collect feedback and update pricing.

Acceptance criteria for GA:
- No regression in premium p99 (>0.5% relative) across pilot pools.
- False eviction rate < 1% of preemption events.
- Micro-reserve cold start avoidance reduces observed p99 spikes by at least 30% on pilot workloads.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Pricing model for micro-reserves vs reserved capacity? (ops/finance input needed)
- How large should credit accrual be for unpredictable bursty customers (burstiness-by-pattern)?
- Is 30s graceful window realistic for batch-heavy workloads? Might need per-route configs.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Priya to prototype credit ledger design (storage schema + API) — DUE: 2024-10-17 (Jira DED-1012).
- Infra to add decision logging events to tracing pipeline (Noah) — stub PR #412.
- Product to draft console UX for opt-in fencing and burst reporting (Marta).

Notes to reviewers: this is purposely lightweight — looking for pragmatic limits and operational knobs rather than a perfect theoretical model. Keep feedback focused on the runbook, observability needs, and acceptance criteria.

Quick links: Slack channel #dedicated-capacity, runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=65789, related design: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
